name: Akara
summary: Crisp-edged, fluffy fritters of whipped black-eyed pea batter, fried until deep golden and best eaten hot.
story: Akara is a popular Nigerian street food and breakfast made from peeled black-eyed peas, blended and whipped before frying. It is commonly eaten with pap (ogi) or soft bread. In parts of Brazil a related fritter, acaraje, is also eaten.

steps.title: Peel the beans
steps.text: Soak the beans for 10 to 15 minutes, then rub them between your hands to loosen the skins. Rinse and pour off the floating skins several times until most are removed.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Blend the beans with the onion and pepper using the minimum water, until the batter is thick, smooth and creamy with no gritty bits.

steps.title: Whip the batter
steps.text: Pour into a bowl and beat vigorously with a wooden spoon or whisk for 5 to 8 minutes until pale, fluffy and slightly increased in volume. Stir in the salt at the end.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Heat the oil in a deep pan to about 180 C (350 F). A drop of batter should sizzle and rise within seconds.

steps.title: Fry in batches
steps.text: Scoop a heaped tablespoon of batter and gently slide it into the oil. Fry 4 to 5 minutes, turning once, until deep golden brown and crisp outside.

steps.title: Drain and serve
steps.text: Lift out and drain on paper towels. Serve hot with pap, bread or a spicy pepper sauce.

tips: Whipping the batter is the secret to light, airy akara.
Add salt at the end; early salt thins the batter.
Keep the oil hot enough; oil that is too cool makes greasy akara.

swaps.swap: Use skinless dried black-eyed peas or ready-made bean flour (ewa flour) mixed with water to save peeling time.
Habanero or a milder red chilli.
